o1.biggest_strength: Separates proved from to-check cleanly and ranks the real money leaks (Meta/linen, switched-off flows) with owners and first-week steps.
o1.biggest_mistake: The payback math ($94 LTV) bakes in assumptions that aren't stress-tested, and the comforter 'too warm' fix is thin; expected order is slightly loose.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Tighten the repeat-value assumption with an actual repeat order value and margin, and quantify each move's gross profit in dollars rather than vague 'medium/high' bands.

o2.biggest_strength: Puts every move in one unit (points of contribution margin) with sizing, lines and stop thresholds, plus a genuinely fresh swatch-kit concept and a sharp brand catch on the 'hotel' line.
o2.biggest_mistake: The contribution baseline (7.8% vs 13.6%) is built on an unstated, fragile solver (w × −11% + (1−w) × 6% = −4%) and stacked assumptions; a couple of projections (5.6-point swatch upside) look optimistic.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Show the baseline working plainly and flag it as an estimate, and trim the optimistic range on the swatch test so the numbers hold up under scrutiny.

reason: Both nail the diagnosis, but Output 2 gives me one ranked unit, dollar-sized savings and stop rules I can run Monday, plus a brand catch that protects us. Its contribution baseline is the shakier part, so I'd use it with a finance check.
